items.name: Winged bean
combinations: young pods stir-fried with coconut (Kerala thoran style)
mature seeds soaked and curried like soybean
garlic-ajwain tempering as legume default
contraindications: mature seeds undercooked (soak and boil well)
items.preparation: Young winged pods cook as a crisp vegetable; mature seeds are protein-dense and need full legume treatment. A whole-plant food of the humid coasts and Northeast.

items.name: Rice bean
combinations: simmered into hill dals (Himalayan/Northeast)
with dry ginger in cold-climate cooking
mixed-bean khichdi
contraindications: weak digestion (as any small hard bean)
items.preparation: Small mung-like hill bean, soaked and simmered into rustic dals. A hardy tribal-belt pulse, closer to mung than to chana in temperament.

items.name: Field bean (avarekalu)
items.prabhava: Karnataka's winter obsession — the avarekalu season reshapes Bengaluru menus for two months; classically nishpava, tasty and vidahi in excess.
combinations: avarekalu uppittu and akki rotti (the seasonal pairings)
hitakida bele (skinned, the refined form)
with coconut and jaggery to soften the vidahi edge
items.preparation: Fresh winter field beans shelled, often skinned (hitakida) for delicacy; cooked with coconut-jaggery balance. Enjoy the season, respect the quantity.

items.name: Red cowpea
combinations: Kerala vanpayar thoran with coconut
with rice gruel (kanji-payar, the Kerala comfort meal)
erissery-style with pumpkin
items.preparation: The red-coated cowpea of the South — earthier than the white, traditionally beside rice kanji as the fisherman's supper. Soak, boil soft, temper with coconut oil and curry leaves.

items.name: Whole pigeon pea
combinations: sprouted and curried (Gujarati tuver style)
fresh green tuver in undhiyu
long soak, ghee-hing tadka
contraindications: vata excess / gas-prone (whole is windier than the split dal)
items.preparation: The unsplit bean behind everyday toor dal — needs overnight soaking and long cooking, or sprouting. Fresh green pigeon peas in winter are its gentlest form.

usda.name: Pigeon peas (red gram), mature seeds, raw

items.name: Urad flour
items.prabhava: Masha milled — the binding, building flour behind papad, vada and imarti; all of urad's brimhana weight, none of its whole-bean fibre.
combinations: papad dough with papad-khar (see urad papad)
fermented into vada and imarti batter
laddoo with ghee in vajikarana-style winter sweets
items.preparation: Fine flour of skinned black gram. Fermentation or the alkaline papad treatment are the traditional ways to lift its density; fried forms are heaviest of all.

items.name: Mace
items.prabhava: The lacy aril of the nutmeg — javitri shares jatiphala's calming, gut-settling nature in a brighter, more fragrant key; biryani's quiet aristocrat.
combinations: with nutmeg in warm milk at night (sleep tradition, pinch doses)
in biryani and korma masalas
in chaturjata-family aromatic blends
contraindications: large doses (myristicin — keep to culinary pinches)
items.preparation: Whole blades toasted briefly or powdered fresh; a little perfumes a whole pot. Like nutmeg, its safety lives in the pinch.

items.name: Black mustard seed
items.prabhava: The crackle that opens Indian cooking — rai popped in hot oil converts its harsh pungency into nutty warmth; raw-ground, it is medicine-grade heat.
combinations: popped in the tadka with curry leaves (the universal opening)
ground with curd in southern pachadis
kasundi-style fermented mustard (Bengal)
contraindications: pitta excess — acidity, skin heat, bleeding tendencies
items.preparation: Always tempered in hot oil until it pops, or ground for deliberate heat. Classical texts respect sarshapa as potent — a spice that behaves like a therapy.

items.name: Yellow mustard seed
combinations: ground into Bengali shorshe pastes (with the black for depth)
in pickling masalas
kasundi and mustard sauces
items.preparation: The milder, larger mustard — gentler than rai but still decisively heating. Soaking before grinding softens the bite in paste work.

items.name: Black cumin
items.prabhava: The mountain cumin — darker, sweeter-scented and gentler than common jeera; the biryani and Kashmiri pulao spice that digests rich rice without shouting.
combinations: whole in biryani and Kashmiri pulao
in punjabi garam masalas
dry-roasted over raita
items.reviewNote: Authored as true black cumin (Bunium persicum, shahi/kala jeera) to avoid duplicating kalonji, which predraft item dravya.onion-seed covers; USDA binding updated accordingly.
items.preparation: Slender dark seeds used whole in rice dishes and rich gravies — a milder aromatic cousin of jiraka, at home wherever ghee-rice needs digesting.

items.name: Caraway seed
combinations: in breads and cheese (its European home)
post-meal seed mixes with fennel
in kahwa-adjacent infusions
contraindications: none significant at culinary doses; medicinal-oil doses need care in pregnancy
items.preparation: The jeera-family carminative of colder lands — chewed after meals or baked into breads. Close kin to jeera and shahi jeera in action: wind-moving, gut-settling.

items.name: Celery seed
items.prabhava: Ajmoda of the pharmacies, radhuni of Bengal — the strongest of the ajwain family; a pinch in shukto or dal moves wind and wakes agni like little else.
combinations: a pinch in Bengali shukto and dals
in ajmodadi churna (classical vata formulation)
tempered whole in mustard oil
items.preparation: Used in pinches, tempered briefly — over-frying turns it acrid. Classical ajmoda earns a place in vata formularies; the kitchen dose is a whisper of the medicine.

items.name: Dried pomegranate seed
items.prabhava: Dadima concentrated — the rare souring agent classical texts smile upon: tangy without inflaming, appetising without acidity's payback.
combinations: ground into chole masala (the Punjabi signature sour)
in stuffing for parathas and kachoris
sprinkled over chaats in place of amchur
contraindications: none significant — the gentlest of the sour spices
items.preparation: Sun-dried wild-pomegranate arils, used whole or ground where tamarind would be too harsh. Classical dadima is tridosha-friendly; its dried seed keeps that grace.

items.name: Kokum rind
items.prabhava: The sour that cools — kokum breaks the rule that amla rasa heats: sol kadhi and kokum sherbet are the Konkan's answers to summer, souring food while settling pitta.
combinations: sol kadhi with coconut milk (the digestive finisher)
in dals and fish curries as tamarind's gentler cousin
kokum sherbet with cumin and salt
items.reviewNote: Folk-culinary consensus treats kokum as cooling (summer sherbets, sol kadhi); some nighantu entries class vrikshamla as ushna like other sours. Authored cooling per dominant regional usage.
items.preparation: Dried purple rinds steeped into curries, kadhis and sherbets — added toward the end of cooking for a clean sour. The Konkan pantry's pitta-safe acid.

items.name: Garcinia fruit
items.prabhava: Kerala's fish-curry sour — smoked kudampuli gives meen curry its dark tang and, by fishing-coast conviction, keeps rich fish digestible.
combinations: in Kerala meen (fish) curry — the defining use
soaked and added early in cooking
with coconut milk bases that need cutting
contraindications: modern HCA-extract supplements carry liver cautions — the food rind at culinary doses does not equal the extract
items.preparation: Sun-dried, smoke-cured rinds soaked and simmered into curries. Sourer and darker than kokum, its cousin — coastal cooking's heavy-duty acid.

items.name: Trikatu spice blend
items.prabhava: The three pungents — ginger, black pepper, pippali in equal parts: the classical deepana-pachana engine that kindles agni, burns ama and carries herbs into the tissues (yogavahi).
combinations: a pinch with honey before meals (kapha protocol)
added to formulations to boost absorption
in warm water for cold-season sluggishness
contraindications: pitta excess — acidity, ulcers, bleeding disorders
items.preparation: Equal parts dry ginger, black pepper and pippali, powdered. Pinch doses with honey or warm water — this is a formulation with a pharmacology, not a table spice.

items.name: Chaturjata spice blend
items.prabhava: The four aromatics — cinnamon, cardamom, tejapatra and nagakeshara: the classical finishing blend that perfumes medicine and food alike while gently warming digestion.
combinations: stirred into avalehas and arishtas (classical role)
pinch over kheer and sweets
in masala chai's ancestral lineage
items.preparation: Equal parts twak, ela, patra and nagakeshara, ground fine and added at the end of preparation — heat scatters its aromatics. The perfumer among the digestive blends.

items.name: Panch phoron
items.prabhava: Bengal's whole-seed pentad — fenugreek, nigella, cumin, radhuni (or mustard) and fennel, popped whole in oil: five carminatives firing at once, each taste represented.
combinations: tempered whole in mustard oil for dals and vegetable chorchoris
with pumpkin and bitter gourds (traditional matches)
never ground — the whole-seed pop is the technique
items.preparation: Equal whole seeds, dropped into smoking-hot oil until they crackle, then the vegetables follow. Bengal's answer to the tadka — broader-spectrum, more bitter-wise.

items.name: Classical garam masala
items.prabhava: Literally 'the heating blend' — cardamom, cinnamon, clove, pepper, cumin and bay assembled to raise the body's warmth; northern winter cooking's thermal engine.
combinations: stirred in at the end of cooking (aromatics survive)
in winter dals, meats and gravies
halved or omitted in summer cooking (traditional sense)
items.preparation: Whole spices dry-roasted and ground in small batches; added late. Its name is its dosage instruction — garam for the cold, not for July.

items.name: Sambar spice blend
combinations: the soul of sambar (see sambar)
rubbed on roast vegetables
in podi-idli style dry chutneys
items.preparation: Coriander, red chili, fenugreek, pepper, cumin and roasted dals ground together — the roasted-dal body distinguishes it from bare chili powders. Fresher is brighter.

items.name: Rasam spice blend
items.prabhava: Pepper-forward and cumin-deep — the powder that turns tamarind water into medicine; rasam podi is deepana-pachana dressed as dinner.
combinations: the engine of rasam (see rasam)
pinch in clear soups for colds
with extra pepper as home cold-remedy (milagu rasam logic)
items.preparation: Black pepper, cumin, coriander, toor dal and chili, roasted and ground coarser than sambar podi. The pepper share decides its potency — grandmothers grind it hot on purpose.

items.name: Chai spice blend
items.prabhava: The kadha that moved into the teacup — ginger, cardamom, cinnamon, clove and pepper: a diluted classical decoction riding on daily tea, warming kapha mornings nationwide.
combinations: boiled with milk tea (the standard vehicle)
heavier on ginger-pepper in monsoon and winter
in warm milk without tea for gentler constitutions
contraindications: pitta excess / acidity (especially on empty stomach with strong tea)
reflux-prone (the tea more than the masala)
items.preparation: Dry ginger, cardamom, cinnamon, clove and black pepper in home-proportions, simmered with the tea. The masala is the medicinal half of the cup; the tannin is the tax.

items.name: Licorice root
items.prabhava: Yashtimadhu — 'sweet stick': classical medhya rasayana, voice-smoother and ulcer-soother; the rare intense sweet that medicine claims from the pantry.
combinations: chewed as sticks for throat and voice
with honey for cough (classical pairing)
in milk decoction for gastric fire without acid
in medhya blends with brahmi
contraindications: hypertension (glycyrrhizin raises blood pressure — significant with regular use)
items.preparation: Root sticks chewed, powdered (1–3 g) or simmered in milk or water. Its sweetness is medicinal strength — the blood-pressure caution is modern, real and dose-dependent.

items.name: Pickled ginger
items.prabhava: The classical pre-meal rite made pantry-stable — ginger with salt (and here, sour) taken before food is Charaka's own appetiser prescription: 'always wholesome before meals'.
combinations: a sliver before meals to rouse agni (the classical use)
beside curd rice and khichdi
with lemon juice and rock salt (the fresh version)
items.preparation: Tender ginger cured in lemon juice and salt (or brine-pickled); the pink blush is the lemon's work. A condiment with a classical job: eat a sliver first, then dine.

items.name: Nigella seed
items.prabhava: Kalonji — the 'blessed seed' of Unani (habbat al-barakah); scattered on naan and sealed into pickles, prized across two medical traditions for immunity and digestion.
combinations: pressed onto naan and kulcha
in panch phoron (one of the five)
in achars — its oil resists spoilage
with honey (Unani morning tradition)
items.preparation: Matte-black teardrop seeds used whole — briefly tempered or baked on. Culinary pinches are food; the pressed oil and gram-doses belong to therapeutics.
